tex_content.html:
For all $\kappa ,\alpha ,\theta >0$ there is $\beta (\kappa ,\alpha ,\theta )<\infty $ such that $R(x)d(x,y_i)^2>\beta $ and $\cangle _x(y_1,y_2)\geq \theta $ imply that $x$ is the center of an $\alpha $-neck and $\cangle _x(y_1,y_2)\geq \pi -\alpha $.
Proof

↗ lem:kl-necklike-behavior-at-infinity-three-dimensional-solution-strong-version-existence-kappa-solutions \sketch Compactness and line splitting give the neck; its cross-section separates the far points and gives the angle estimate.

□
Corollary
[existence for kappa solutions]
